body:
A web application may use signed data is several places, for example for the [password reset token](https://www.sjoerdlangkemper.nl/2016/04/07/djangos-reset-password-mechanism/). If the application signs user data in multiple places, it should take care that a piece of signed data from one place cannot be used in another place.

For example, a signed session token should not be usable in the password reset functionality.

comments.body:
In relation to signing session tokens...

Signing only parents tampering of a session ID.  But I can often reuse that session artifact for other features of the same application - it’s very rare for a session to be tied to a specific feature so I disagree with this comment.

--
Jim Manico
@Manicode

I think CVE-2020-15098 is an example of what I mean. In [the fix](https://github.com/TYPO3/TYPO3.CMS/commit/85d3e70dff35a99ef53f4b561114acfa9e5c47e1) you can see that they used `GeneralUtility::hmac` to sign things. In some places, they sign user input and show the result on the page. This creates a signing oracle that makes it possible for an attacker to sign any data.

The solution is to sign for a specific purpose, so that is why they added `'backend-link-browser'` to the HMAC.
Can we get a PR or some more discussion on this? A JWT is signed and gets constantly reused by design...

I have some troubles wording this. I think the purpose of the signed data should be clear. Something like this:

> Verify that signed data is only valid for a specific purpose, so that signed data provided by the web application cannot be used outside of the context it was provided for.

A JWT is of course constantly reused for the purpose of authentication requests, and that's fine. However, if a site also uses JWTs as password reset tokens, the JWTs for authentication and the JWTs for password reset shouldn't be interchangeable.
I'm a little hesitant on this one, if conflicts with other signature designs and I'd like to get more specific instead of a more general requirement like this if possible!

The issue of re-using a secret like a one-time secret for password reset has nothing to do with signature, it's just about not resuing something that is meant to only be used once. So I suggest we change the title of this - because it's otherwise very valid.
@Sjord what are the next steps on this issue? Did you need to prepare a PR or paste a sample wording here?
@Sjord any other comments? Otherwise I will close this mid-may.
